title: The Kindly Bell
premise: Bram Oyelaran returns to the family house in Hollowmere to bury their twin, Wren — except Wren is standing at the funeral, alive, and insists Bram is the one who died. The house's mirrors begin lagging a second behind reality, and in that stolen second Bram glimpses the Kindly Bell, an old parish bell that once rang to settle debts the law wouldn't touch. As the lag widens and family members start vanishing into reflections, Bram learns the twins' grandmother struck a bargain: one Oyelaran twin owed to the bell each generation. To save the family, Bram must finally believe — and choose whether love or duty answers when the bell counts to twelve.
about_author: O. M. Nystrom is the pen name of a former church archivist who spent years cataloguing parish records of unexplained deaths in coastal villages. They write horror about families that keep terrible promises, and they still refuse to own a mirror larger than a handkerchief.

chapters.title: The Wrong Grave
chapters.summary: Bram arrives in Hollowmere for Wren's funeral and finds Wren waiting at the graveside, insisting Bram is the dead twin. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: disorientation and grief curdling into denial as the town's mourners greet Bram like a ghost.

chapters.title: House of Kept Things
chapters.summary: Bram moves into the family house, where every room holds objects no one will explain — especially the sealed parlor. Aunt Sable warns them not to look at anything too long. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: unease beneath forced normalcy; belonging offered on strange terms.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Bram notices the hallway mirror reflecting their movements a beat behind. Testing it with Wren, they confirm the lag is real and growing. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: rationalist dread — the first crack in a lifetime of disbelief.

chapters.title: Wren's Version
chapters.summary: Wren recounts the night of the accident from the other side: Bram went through the ice, Wren pulled out a body wearing Bram's coat. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: tender, furious sibling intimacy strained by impossible facts.

chapters.title: The Bell Registry
chapters.summary: In the parish archive, Bram finds the registry of the Kindly Bell — names paired across generations, always two siblings, always one struck through. Their grandmother's handwriting marks both twins' names. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: cold clarity; justice outside the law has a ledger.

chapters.title: Sable's Silence
chapters.summary: Bram confronts Aunt Sable, who admits the family has paid the bell for six generations but refuses to say what happens at the count. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: guilt worn as duty; love expressed only as withholding.

chapters.title: The Lag Widens
chapters.summary: The mirror delay stretches to five seconds; Bram watches their reflection keep moving after they stop. Cousin Ivo swears he saw someone else in the glass. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: escalating panic masked by methodical note-taking.

chapters.title: Ivo Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Ivo stops speaking mid-sentence at dinner; his reflection remains at the table, smiling, long after he's gone. The family pretends nothing happened. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: horror of complicity — the household's practiced blindness.

chapters.title: What the Bell Settles
chapters.summary: Digging into parish records, Bram learns the bell rang for crimes the village courts excused — and took payment in people instead of verdicts. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: grim understanding that Hollowmere's peace was purchased.

chapters.title: The Sealed Parlor
chapters.summary: Bram breaks into the parlor and finds the original bell rope, a wall of portraits with scratched-out faces, and grandmother's contract: one twin per generation, freely given. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: betrayal — belonging was always collateral.

chapters.title: Counting to Nine
chapters.summary: The mirrors begin showing a countdown etched backwards in the glass. At nine chimes heard by everyone, the house's doors seal themselves. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: claustrophobic unity — the family trapped together with its debt.

chapters.title: Sable's Confession
chapters.summary: Sable reveals she was meant to be the payment forty years ago; her sister volunteered instead, and the bell accepted — then waited. She believes it wants both twins now. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: Through the Glass
chapters.summary: Bram reaches into a mirror and touches the reflected parlor — solid, cold, smelling of river water. Something on the other side touches back. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: terror giving way to awful curiosity; belief arriving against their will.

chapters.title: The Drowned Twin
chapters.summary: In the glass world, Bram meets the previous generation's payment — their aunt, unchanged since 1984, who explains the bell keeps what it's owed unless something better is offered. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: compassion for the kept; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren secretly offers themself to the bell to end it, believing Bram is already dead and this is mercy. The countdown jumps to eleven. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: love against duty — sacrifice disguised as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Family Meeting
chapters.summary: The surviving family argues over who owes what; old resentments surface as each confesses a small cruelty the bell might collect. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: bitter catharsis — honesty as survival strategy.

chapters.title: Eleven Chimes
chapters.summary: The eleventh chime takes the house's light and Sable's voice. In every mirror, the family sees themselves as the bell sees them: entries in a ledger. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: desolation before defiance.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Hour
chapters.summary: Bram drags Wren to the parlor as the twelfth chime begins, planning to break the rope and void the contract — knowing it may take them both. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: resolve born of love, not belief in rules.

chapters.title: What Bram Offers
chapters.summary: At the rope, Bram offers the bell something unprecedented: not a twin, but the truth — public testimony of every crime it ever settled, ending its usefulness. The bell hesitates between payment and purpose. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: climax; disbelief weaponized into justice.

chapters.title: The Bell Answers
chapters.summary: The bell accepts the testimony and rings once for itself — a sound that unmakes the mirrors and releases everything it kept, including the aunt, aged forty years in a breath. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: awe and grief entwined; freedom that costs.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unmirrored
chapters.summary: The family buries the empty coffin properly and covers every mirror with cloth, then removes them entirely. Bram and Wren, neither sure which of them died, choose to be both alive. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: fragile reconciliation; belonging rebuilt without ledgers.

chapters.title: A Ringing Far Off
chapters.summary: Months later, leaving Hollowmere, Bram hears — or imagines — a single distant chime and does not turn around. Some debts are settled; some bells simply wait. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: quiet, earned ambiguity; walking forward anyway.
